semantics.label: Task assistant
semantics.description: Start from a complete example task or check the task for common mistakes. A template is previewed before it replaces the assignment settings.

fields.label: Select...
fields.description: Select database

fields.label: Upload type

fields.label: Database
fields.description: SQLite database file

fields.label: SQL file
fields.description: SQL file that creates and fills the database.

fields.label: SQL import options
fields.description: Options for uploaded SQL files.

fields.label: Clean MySQL dump
fields.description: Remove common MySQL dump syntax before importing into SQLite.

fields.label: Repository manifest URL
fields.description: URL of a JSON manifest that lists externally hosted SQLQuestion databases.

fields.label: Database name
fields.description: Database id from the repository manifest.

fields.label: Type
fields.description: Select predefined Database

semantics.label: Content
semantics.description: Text can contain text, images, videos and code

fields.label: Type
fields.description: Type of H5P Content

fields.label: Text
fields.description: Write general description as markdown code

fields.label: Image
fields.description: An optional image appended to instructions

fields.label: Show Editor?
fields.description: Should an editor displayed to the user

fields.label: Player mode
fields.description: The code is only played: no editor is shown, learners just run it and see the output (console, canvas, ...). Requires 'Show Editor?' to be enabled.

fields.label: Offer 'Show code' button
fields.description: In player mode, learners can reveal the code with a button. If disabled, the code stays hidden.

fields.label: Code
fields.description: Write general description as markdown code

fields.label: External Library URLs (YAML)
fields.description:
Optional YAML map for overriding hosted runtime libraries in one place. Leave empty to use the defaults.

Example with default values:
blockly: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/blockly@12.4.1/
codeMirror: ""
markdown: https://esm.sh/
fontAwesome: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/@fortawesome/fontawesome-free@6.4.0/css/all.min.css
sweetAlert: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/sweetalert2-uncensored@11.10.8-1-uncensored/dist/sweetalert2.all.min.js
jsZip: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/jszip@3.10.1/dist/jszip.min.js
sqlJs: https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/sql.js@1.8.0/dist/

semantics.label: Editor Settings
semantics.description: This defines how the actual editor is pre-populated and whether code should be executed before or after user input.

fields.label: Instructions
fields.description: Write instructions as markdown code

fields.label: Instructions Image
fields.description: An optional image appended to instructions

fields.label: Default Code
fields.description: Add default code here, so that learners can modify this code.

fields.label: Player mode
fields.description: The code is only played: no editor is shown, learners just run it and see the output (console, canvas, ...).

fields.label: Offer 'Show code' button
fields.description: In player mode, learners can reveal the code with a button. If disabled, the code stays hidden.

fields.label: Editor mode
fields.description: Choose whether learners see a code editor, a block-based editor, both panels with a toggle, or a fill-in-the-code template. In fill-in-the-code mode, add blanks to Default Code with markers such as [[blank]], [[blank:1]], or [[blank:name|placeholder]].

semantics.label: Grading Settings
semantics.description: Information how the content should be graded

fields.label: Grading method
fields.description: How the learner's answer is graded.

fields.label: Solution query
fields.description: Reference query whose result learners have to reproduce. Warning: it can be seen in the website source code.

fields.label: Result comparison
fields.description: How strictly the learner's result table is compared with the result of the solution query. The defaults accept any row order but require identical column names.

fields.label: Row order
fields.description: Choose "Rows must be in the same order" for tasks that require ORDER BY.

options.label: Rows must be in the same order

fields.label: Columns
fields.description: "Only values count" accepts different aliases (AS) as long as the column count and the values match.

options.label: Names must match, order does not matter

fields.label: Ignore letter case
fields.description: Compare text values and column names without distinguishing upper and lower case.

fields.label: Numeric tolerance
fields.description: Numbers that differ by at most this value count as equal, for example 0.01 for rounded averages. 0 requires exact values.

fields.label: Query requirements
fields.description: Structural requirements for the learner's query text. They apply to every test case, in addition to the result comparison.

fields.label: Required keywords
fields.description: Comma-separated SQL keywords the query must contain, for example: JOIN, GROUP BY.

fields.label: Forbidden keywords
fields.description: Comma-separated SQL keywords the query must not contain, for example: LIMIT, DISTINCT.

fields.label: Forbid subqueries
fields.description: Reject queries that contain a nested SELECT.

fields.label: Forbid SELECT *
fields.description: Learners have to name the columns. COUNT(*) is still allowed.

fields.label: Award partial credit
fields.description: Award each passed test case its weight in points. Disabled: all test cases have to pass for the full score.

fields.label: Test Cases
fields.description: Optional data variants. Each test case runs the solution query and the learner query on the database plus the setup SQL of the test case and compares the results. This detects answers that only work for the visible data. The default database is always tested as the first test case.

fields.label: Test name
fields.description: For example: additional country or empty table. Hidden test names are not displayed.

fields.label: Learning goal
fields.description: Tests with the same learning goal are summarized together. Hidden tests are excluded from this summary.

fields.label: Hint after failure
fields.description: A specific next step shown when this visible test fails.

fields.label: Points for this test
fields.description: Used when partial credit is enabled.

fields.label: Hidden Testcase
fields.description: The data and results of this test are not shown to learners.

fields.label: Setup SQL
fields.description: SQL that is executed on the database before the solution and the learner query run, for example INSERT statements that add rows. Leave empty to test the unchanged database.

fields.label: Multiple Choice
fields.description: Use Markdown for answer options. Code fences and Mermaid/UML diagrams are supported when the Markdown renderer is available.

fields.label: Allow multiple correct answers
fields.description: If enabled, learners can select several answer options.

fields.label: Randomize answer order
fields.description: If enabled, the order of the answer options is shuffled for each learner.

fields.label: Answer text
fields.description: Write the answer option as Markdown. You can use code fences or Mermaid diagrams.

semantics.label: Hint Cascade
semantics.description: Didactic hints that learners can reveal one by one after the first wrong answer. Order them from conceptual to strategic to a partial solution.

fields.label: Enable hint button
fields.description: Shows a hint button after the first wrong answer. Each click reveals the next hint below. Hint usage is reported via xAPI.

fields.label: Hints
fields.description: First hint: conceptual nudge. Second: strategy. Last: closest to the solution.

semantics.label: Worked Example
semantics.description: After repeated failed checks, a fully worked solution is offered for study.

fields.label: Enable worked example
fields.description: Reveals the worked example below the task after the configured number of failed checks.

fields.label: Reveal after failed checks
fields.description: Number of failed checks after which the worked example appears.

fields.label: Worked example code
fields.description: The complete solution, ideally with explanatory SQL comments.
